newsitem.title: UK: English cricket captain stars in Queen's honours.
newsitem.headline: English cricket captain stars in Queen's honours.

text.p: England cricket captain Mike Atherton topped Queen Elizabeth's birthday honours list on Saturday while gallantry awards were given to teachers involved in the Dunblane school massacre and to murdered headmaster Philip Lawrence.
Atherton becomes an officer of the Order of the British Empire (OBE) in recognition of his dogged efforts to pull a largely unsuccessful team up by the bootstraps over the last four years.

It marks his complete rehabilitation after he was almost forced to resign three years ago amid ball-tampering allegations, a heinous crime in the cricket world. Last week, England won the first match of a six-test "Ashes" series against Australia.

Lawrence, who was stabbed to death by a 16-year-old youth in west London while trying to help one of his pupils, was posthumously awarded the Queen's Gallantry Medal while Gwen Mayor and two other Dunblane teachers were given the Queen's Commendation for Bravery, Mayor posthumously.
Last year, 16 children and Mayor, their teacher, were gunned down in a school gymnasium in the small Scottish town by crazed loner Thomas Hamilton. He later shot himself.
Several months later, another school tragedy was narrowly averted when a man obsessed by the Dunblane massacre attacked children in a nursery school playground in the Midlands.

None of the children was killed thanks to nursery nurse Lisa Potts, 22, who was seriously injured by blows from the attacker's md the George Medal for bravery. Only 23 such medals have been awarded in the past 10 years.
Other sportsmen to receive recognition included one of Atherton's predecessors as cricket captain, Colin Cowdrey.
He becomes a life peer while umpire David Shepherd becomes a member of the British Empire (MBE). Walter Smith, manager of Glasgow Rangers football club, receives an OBE.
Peter O'Sullevan, a horse racing broadcaster who has been the voice of racing to millions of fans, was knighted.
So too was veteran character actor Donald Sinden, teased remorselessly in the 1980s by satirical television programme Spitting Image for constantly angling for a knighthood.
Playwright Tom Stoppard also received a knighthood while jazz singer Cleo Laine was made a Dame of the British Empire.
Maverick British painter David Hockney, who recently returned to Britae United States, is made a Companion of Honour.

Born in the northern town of Bradford nearly 60 years ago, the pop-art pioneer says he left for the U.S. in search of light. "Every morning the sun shines in California. I like it, because for the first 20 years of my lredesign its livery.
Nick Park, creator of multiple Oscar-winning animated film characters Wallace and Gromit, becomes a Commander of the Order of the British Empire (CBE).

In all, 980 civil awards were on the list of recommendations, drawn up by Conservative prime minister John Major before his defeat in the May 1 general election. His Labour successor, Tony Blair, submitted the to its word, and as part of its proclaimed effort to "clean up" government, Labour did not proceed with any of the political nominations put forward. The nearest thing to a political honour was the MBE given to Bob Jordan, doorkeeper at No. 10 Downing Street, the prime minister's residence.
Major has yet to submit his traditional "Resignation Honours" list which could include many of the politicians omitted by Blair.
